data.narrative: The student demonstrated executive engineering poise and disciplined mid-flight adaptation under high pressure in Module 07. Faced with sudden corporate account requirements and a timeline compressed to 6 days for an investor demo, they mapped blast radius across 11 artifacts, preserved completed investments without panic, and restructured the execution plan into clear Preserved, Modified, Cut, and Added categories. When a second requirement change (hierarchical 3-tier RBAC) arrived 15 minutes later, they avoided starting over or relying on heroic overtime; instead, they evolved their minimal bridge into pragmatic enum-based roles, made calculated scope cuts (demoting email notifications to in-app receipts), and maintained credible, transparent stakeholder communications.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted the deep architectural implications of corporate booking delegation and 3-tier RBAC (manager, employee, department head), mapping entity relationships and row-level scoping requirements.
dimension_scores.evidence: Detailed role permissions and schema extensions in artifacts/adaptation/module-07-blast-radius.md and progress/decomposition/module-07-break.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Audited dependency topologies before cutting scope, proving that Google Calendar sync and reviews were strict leaf nodes that could be removed without destabilizing core booking transactions.
Rejected the dangerous 'work harder / work faster' trap, recognizing that adding 4 days of work to a halved timeline requires decisive scope cuts rather than uncalculated developer crunch.
dimension_scores.evidence: Categorized not-started tickets into MUST SHIP, SHOULD SHIP, and CUT in artifacts/adaptation/module-07-blast-radius.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Authored crisp, actionable ticket modifications and additions with explicit sizing (S/M/L) that an engineer could pick up and execute without ambiguity.
dimension_scores.evidence: Structured revised ticket backlog with acceptance criteria in artifacts/adaptation/module-07-updated-plan.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Layered two back-to-back requirement changes seamlessly without throwing away in-flight progress or resetting the project to zero.
dimension_scores.evidence: Produced v1 and v2 layered adaptations in progress/decomposition/module-07-fix.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Evolved a brittle boolean flag into an enum-based pragmatic RBAC model, hitting the sweet spot between a 3-week full rewrite and an unscalable hack.

strengths: Demonstrated exceptional mid-flight adaptation under compressed deadlines, treating the execution plan as a living navigation system.
Principled scope management: traded leaf-node features (calendar sync, email receipts) to absorb critical enterprise security requirements without date slippage.
High-maturity stakeholder communication that clearly states what will ship, what is deferred, and what is required from leadership.

public_evidence.technical_detail: Blast radius matrix, Preserved/Modified/Cut/Added categorization, Pragmatic RBAC architecture, and PM impact statement.
public_evidence.proof: Delivered coherent v2 execution plan preserving completed work while absorbing two major enterprise requirement shifts within a 6-day investor demo constraint.
public_evidence.ability: Adapts engineering plans under changing requirements, protects deadlines with principled scope cuts, and communicates transparently with stakeholders.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates tech lead and engineering manager poise: avoids both panic-restarts and burnout-inducing scope stuffing, keeping delivery predictable under volatility.
